espn-603996.headline: Fourth time in 16 months, and Twickenham may make it five
beats: Wales have won two of the three meetings since July 2025. The last, in Cardiff on 15 November 2025, went 24–23 with a last-gasp finish and gave Steve Tandy his first Test win.
Wales have not played since July, when they lost 21–35 in Argentina and then 0–43 in South Africa without a try. Japan come in off a 28–34 home defeat to Fiji, scoring four tries and still losing.
Japan have beaten Wales twice, but never in Cardiff. Doing it here would lift them above Wales and Italy, and leave Wales 12th at best.

Next, Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England. The finals weekend pairs ninth with tenth, and they are ninth and tenth now, a point apart, so the winner in Cardiff may only have earned another go.

sources.title: Japan date starts pivotal month for Welsh rugby

espn-603997.headline: Dupont and Ntamack start together. It has been a while
beats: Antoine Dupont and Romain Ntamack start together at half-back for the first time since March 2025. Dupont missed all of July with a calf issue. Ntamack's injuries include a long-running kidney problem.

France managed without them in July. They lost 34–32 to New Zealand, then put 42 on both Australia and Japan. The injury list has grown since, and an uncapped loose forward, Esteban Capilla, is on the bench.

Jake White's second game in charge of Fiji brings a Test debut for Nathan Hughes, a former England international. England scored 73 against Fiji in July. A Fiji win by 15 or fewer would drop France to fifth in the world, below England.
South Africa are in France next. Galthié would like his half-backs to have met by then.

espn-603998.headline: One side backs its coach, the other argues about pay
beats: Steve Borthwick has the full support of his bosses, which is rarely said of a coach who is safe. His players have denied rumours of a rift after England's worst-ever Six Nations. Australia arrive in a pay dispute.

Under Les Kiss, Australia won five of his first seven, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in a fortnight. England won here 25–7 last November. Ugo Monye thinks they play best with their backs to the wall, and that the danger is the ill discipline that has plagued them of late.
Fin Smith is fit at fly-half after a calf injury. Ben Curry replaces his injured twin Tom. Fraser McReight wins his 50th cap.
Win, and Australia take England's fifth place in the world rankings, with England dropping below Scotland as well. Australia go to Scotland next, so one row would have a short shelf life.

espn-603999.headline: France can make New Zealand world No. 1 in Saint-Denis
beats: South Africa won 32–17 at the Stade de France last November. They arrive five points clear at the top of the Nations Championship, four wins from four. A France win would cost them first place in the world rankings, and New Zealand would take it.
New Zealand beat France 34–32 in Christchurch in July. That France side was missing its Toulouse and Montpellier players.

Rassie Erasmus picked his strongest available side against Italy and held back his uncapped youngsters. Victor Matfield expects some of them to play in the harder games. Against France or Ireland, he says, Erasmus "doesn't mind giving those players an opportunity."
South Africa play Ireland away a week later. New Zealand are not playing in Saint-Denis, and have the most to gain from it.

espn-604000.headline: Italy have no points; Argentina have one win all year
beats: Italy sit last of twelve in the Nations Championship, four played, four lost and 153 points down. Their last win was 23–18 over England at home in March.
Argentina are hardly flush. They have won one Test in seven this year, and in Dublin on 6 November Ireland scored six of the eight tries in a 42–12 win, with the Argentine pack disrupted throughout.
Win in Genova and Italy go up to ninth in the world, above Fiji and Wales. Fiji are the other side without a point, and they are in Italy on 21 November.
Argentina go to France that same day. That is no place to arrive still looking for a reset.

espn-604001.headline: Seventy-two years, and a hat trick didn't dent it
beats: When New Zealand won 52-26 in Cardiff on 22 November 2025, it extended a winning run over Wales that had already reached 72 years. Tom Rogers became the first Wales player to score a hat trick against them that day. New Zealand still scored seven tries.
Wales' last Test was in July, a 43-0 defeat by South Africa without a try. New Zealand lost three straight to the same opponents, then scored 50 and 43 against Australia in October.

Win, and Wales climb above Fiji to ninth in the world. New Zealand stay second whatever happens, but they are level on points with Ireland in the Nations Championship and travel to England a week later.
Steve Tandy has called this a pivotal November for Welsh rugby. Seventy-two years suggests this is the hardest part of it to pivot.

espn-604002.headline: Japan can move the one thing England have kept still
beats: England have been fifth in every world ranking since 13 July. That covers their worst-ever Six Nations and a year with more defeats than wins. Japan were ninth until they lost 28–34 at home to Fiji on 24 October, a month after beating the same side 20–15.
England's last two Tests were July wins away to Fiji and Argentina, 73–8 and 31–24. A Japan win in London would lift them to ninth and drop England to seventh, below Scotland and Australia.

Jamie George says the squad are "really upset" by a report of player unrest over Steve Borthwick's leadership at the end of the summer tour. Borthwick's bosses have backed him, which is not a sentence anyone needs when things are going well.
England host New Zealand a week later, and Japan go to Scotland. Fifth is easier to hold than to win back.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland have nothing to win against Fiji but the game
beats: Ireland are third in the world, and a win by any margin leaves them exactly there. A draw is enough to put France above them.

They come off six tries and a 42–12 win over Argentina, after which Andy Farrell said they could have been more ruthless. Fiji conceded 73 to England in July and have no Nations Championship points, though they did win in Japan last month, 34–28.
Joey Carbery won the last of his 38 caps against Fiji, in 2022. His road back runs through Fiji A, with an Ireland XV in Cork on 20 November.
A week after this, South Africa bring four wins from four to Dublin. Fiji go to Italy, the only side below them, and that is the easier of their two games.

espn-604004.headline: Scotland score 50 to win; Australia have conceded it
beats: Scotland's wins this year include 47–38 in Argentina and 50–40 against France at Murrayfield. Australia's last two games were against New Zealand, and they conceded 50 and 43 in a week. They also have England at Twickenham to get through first, in the middle of a pay dispute.
Sixth hosts seventh, with almost nothing between them. An Australian win by any margin puts them above Scotland.

Gregor Townsend once spent an amateur summer in Sydney playing for Warringah. Scotland have won 13 of 35 meetings with Australia, yet this fixture has produced some of the most scintillating rugby of his nine years in charge.
Scotland host Japan next, and Australia go to Wales. Whoever loses will at least know what to work on.

espn-604005.headline: Beating New Zealand by 14 is no longer enough
beats: England beat New Zealand 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. To climb to third in the world, above Ireland and France, they need to do it again by two points more.
England's year began with their worst-ever Six Nations campaign, a defeat by Italy included. It has since steadied with wins over Fiji and Argentina, the second away in July.
New Zealand lost three in a row to South Africa, conceding 43 in the last of them. They then put 50 and 43 on Australia in October.
England have already lost to South Africa by 24 in this competition. New Zealand have lost to them three times this year and are still unbeaten in it.

espn-604006.headline: Jack Dempsey gets an early look at his new address
beats: Jack Dempsey says a move to Japan will keep him fresh and hungry through the long build-up to next year's World Cup. Now the Scotland No 8's side get Japan at Murrayfield.

He also says Scotland can be the best and worst team in the world. Their year agrees: 50–40 over France at home, then beaten 43–21 by Ireland a week later. They have conceded 38 or more in four of their last five.

Japan have their own split personality. They beat Fiji 20–15 in September, then lost to them 34–28 at home in October, and slid from 9th to 12th in the world. Win in Edinburgh and they are straight back up to 9th.
Either way, Dempsey's new hosts will have an opinion on the result.
